children.text: Heritage Cedar offers molded shingle, shake and rounded-edge profiles with texture between individual shingles as well as on the face. The choice of edge pattern changes the character of a gable or accent wall; thickness varies by profile.

Vortex Extreme combines a .046-inch panel with a reinforced fastening and locking design. Extended lengths can reduce visible joints on wide walls, while the split-cedar appearance keeps the courses visually textured.

Variform Board & Batten uses an extra-thick .048-inch panel for a vertical board-and-batten look. Use the repeated raised battens to emphasize height on a gable or carry one consistent pattern across a full elevation.

Camden Pointe combines a .044-inch panel with cedar texture and pronounced shadow lines. Its rollover panel lock and nail hem are part of the attachment design, alongside the profile and color choices that shape the finished wall.

American Herald uses .044-inch panels with the appearance of natural sawn cedar. Through-panel color helps make surface scratches less conspicuous, while the nail hem and panel lock provide the intended attachment arrangement.

Ashton Heights uses .042-inch vinyl panels with a double-staggered nail hem. It offers a different panel specification from Camden Pointe, so compare the actual profile and attachment details alongside the shared color palette.

Contractor’s Choice is a .040-inch vinyl line for traditional horizontal siding. Compare course width, matching corners and trim before choosing it, since those details determine the proportions of the wall as much as the color does.

Victoria Harbor uses a six-and-a-half-inch beaded face to create a traditional horizontal pattern. Its brushed finish and full bead produce a cleaner, finer shadow detail than deeply embossed cedar-grain siding.

LP SmartSide Lap Siding uses treated engineered wood in long horizontal boards. Cedar texture emphasizes grain; Brushed Smooth creates a quieter painted surface. Primed boards allow custom paint, while ExpertFinish provides a factory-applied color option.

LP SmartSide Trim & Fascia frames windows, corners and roof edges in treated engineered wood. Board width and thickness affect the depth of those transitions, so trim needs to be selected alongside the siding and soffit.
LP SmartSide Nickel Gap creates a defined narrow reveal between boards. Cedar and Brushed Smooth textures let that repeated joint read as rustic or contemporary, with primed and prefinished choices.

LP SmartSide Soffit finishes the underside of the roof overhang. Cedar and Brushed Smooth textures coordinate with the wall finish, while the soffit selection also needs to preserve the roof’s planned intake ventilation.

LP SmartSide Panel & Vertical Siding creates broad wall surfaces that can be detailed with trim for a board-and-batten effect. Panel joints, flashing and trim placement should be coordinated so the finished pattern and drainage work together.

Hardie Panel creates broad vertical fiber-cement surfaces. Smooth, wood-textured and stucco-like options offer different appearances, and added battens can create a farmhouse pattern without changing the panel material.

Hardie Artisan uses extra-thick fiber-cement boards and deep shadow lines for a more pronounced architectural finish. The line is primed for paint, making the final coating and joint treatment part of the design decision.

Hardie Shingle gives fiber cement a cedar-shake appearance. Straight-edge panels create an orderly course, while staggered-edge panels make the silhouette more irregular; either can distinguish a gable from the main lap siding.

Hardie Architectural Panel uses contemporary textures and clean panel lines for an intentional facade pattern. It is primed for your paint color, so panel layout, expressed joints and the finish should be designed together.

Hardie Trim Batten Boards create the raised vertical strips in a board-and-batten exterior. They pair with Hardie Panel, with smooth or textured surfaces to coordinate the battens and the wall behind them.

children.text: DoublePro is a dual-layer continuous hanger installed with new gutters. It combines gutter support and debris screening in one system, making it a different choice from a screen added later to an existing gutter.

T-Rex is a continuous hanger that supports a new gutter along its length rather than at individual hanger points. Its perforated cover also screens debris; gutter pitch, outlets and downspout capacity still determine the drainage route.

Gutter Clean Pro is a retrofit guard for suitable existing gutters. Its Flex-Seal rear detail helps close the space behind the guard, while the screening surface reduces debris entry into the gutter trough.
Gutter Clean is an aluminum debris-screening option for existing gutters. It does not replace assessment of gutter condition, slope or downspouts; repair those issues before selecting a guard.

children.text: Cedar Dimensions uses molded polypropylene panels to create the irregular edges and grain associated with cedar shingles and shakes. The family includes straight shingle, hand-split shake and half-round looks, so it can be used to change the character of a gable, porch or full wall rather than simply change its color.

The profiles are separate panels with their own dimensions and matching corner pieces. Nominal thickness ranges from .080 to .100 inch across the family. A Double 7 shingle and a Double 9 shake should not be treated as interchangeable when calculating quantities or ordering trim.

Choose the panel profile before the accessories. Ply Gem lists dedicated cedar-panel starter strips and profile-specific corners; those details give the wall a more convincing finish than using an unrelated lap-siding accessory. Color availability also varies by profile.

Dimensions is the .044-inch nominal-thickness lap siding in the Ply Gem Performance Collection. Its ⅝-inch profile creates a deeper shadow line, making the individual courses more defined across a broad wall. The folded nail hem and oversized lock are parts of the panel design rather than added accessories.

Choose Double 4 traditional lap for a straightforward clapboard look or Double 4½ Dutch lap for a beveled course with a more pronounced shadow. The profiles have different panel lengths, which matters when planning seams around windows, corners and long wall runs.

Compare a full sample against the trim and roof color outdoors. The family palette includes solid and cedar-inspired finishes, but the chosen color still needs to be checked against the exact panel profile. Thickness alone is not a whole-wall wind rating; fastening and the supporting wall also matter.

Progressions combines a fine-grained, painted-wood appearance with .042-inch nominal-thickness vinyl panels. Its ½-inch profile gives the courses definition without using the deeper profile of Dimensions. It is a useful family to compare when you want several lap-width choices in one collection.

The four profiles include Double 4 and Double 5 traditional lap plus Double 4½ and Double 5 Dutch lap. A wider exposure changes the number of horizontal lines across the wall; Dutch lap adds a beveled shadow at the top of each course. Those differences are more useful to judge on a full sample than on a small color chip.

Panel length and color selection vary by profile. Plan the preferred exposure, seams and corner details together, then compare the exact product in the installation estimate. Darker colors are not necessarily available across every Progressions profile.

Performance Board + Batten creates vertical lines with a 5½-inch board face and a 1½-inch batten. It can emphasize the height of a gable or become the main exterior pattern. The .048-inch nominal panel thickness and 9⁄16-inch profile distinguish it from the horizontal lap products in the collection.

Ply Gem lists a 10-foot panel length. On taller walls, horizontal breaks and transitions need to be designed rather than left as an incidental seam. The way the vertical panels meet a roofline, window head or lower siding material affects both the appearance and the drainage detail.

Starting and finishing a vertical panel is different from starting horizontal lap siding. Match the base channel, corners and opening details to this panel orientation. Review the color on a physical sample, especially where board-and-batten will sit beside another siding profile.

Transformations is the .040-inch nominal-thickness lap siding family in the Ply Gem Performance Collection. A ½-inch profile and defined locking system provide a familiar clapboard or Dutch-lap appearance. Its smaller family color palette makes it a straightforward starting point for a conventional exterior.

Choose Double 4 or Double 5 traditional lap for flat course lines, or Double 4½ Dutch lap for a beveled shadow. These options differ in exposure and panel length, so the profile should be identified by name in the product selection rather than described only as vinyl siding.

Discuss wall preparation, flashing, trim and fastening alongside the panel. A lower nominal thickness does not remove those installation steps. The finished result depends on the complete wall assembly, including the condition behind the old siding and how the new panels connect at openings and edges.

SturdiPlank S7 uses a single seven-inch exposure instead of multiple narrow courses molded into one panel. The wider face and three-quarter-inch projection give horizontal walls a more substantial clapboard rhythm.

Cedar Knolls brings a hand-cut cedar appearance to .044-inch vinyl siding. Its five-eighths-inch projection and three profile choices make it useful for coordinating different wall widths without changing the overall material.

Rustic Hill is a polypropylene shake-and-shingle family, rather than conventional horizontal PVC siding. Cape Cod shingles, traditional shakes and hand-split shakes have different textures and panel thicknesses, making them distinct choices for gables or full walls.

secondary.title: A natural surface that changes outdoors
secondary.copy: Exposure changes wood’s appearance. A transparent or semi-transparent outdoor finish can retain visible grain, while unfinished cedar develops a weathered surface; neither choice removes the need for cleaning and inspection.

secondary.title: Finish dry, prepared boards
secondary.copy: Cedar’s surface condition affects how evenly a coating absorbs. Dry new boards may be finished immediately; weathered surfaces need suitable preparation before a new finish is applied.

secondary.title: Plan care alongside the design
secondary.copy: Sun, rain and foot traffic affect the coating. Choose an exterior deck finish and maintenance plan for the look you want to keep, then coordinate the deck details with Roof King.

secondary.title: Match treatment to exposure
secondary.copy: Above-ground deck boards and members exposed to ground contact can require different treatment ratings. Identify the intended use on the lumber tag rather than assuming every treated board has the same protection.

secondary.title: Use compatible connections
secondary.copy: Treated lumber requires corrosion-resistant fasteners and connectors selected for the preservative and exposure. Compatible hardware helps protect the connections that carry the deck’s loads.

secondary.title: Make room for wood movement and care
secondary.copy: Moisture changes can affect board dimensions and finish readiness. Plan board spacing, drainage and coating preparation around the material supplied, and include ongoing cleaning and inspection in your maintenance plan.

children.text: Trex Signature decking emphasizes a finely detailed natural appearance in composite boards. It is a separate decking product from Trex Signature railing; confirm current local supply and the exact decking specification before planning a new project.

Trex Transcend Lineage offers a refined grain pattern in seven colors with SunComfortable technology. Its heat-mitigating design is compared with Trex’s original boards; the surface can still become hot in direct sunlight.

Trex Transcend combines a pronounced wood-grain surface with five multi-tonal colors. The protective shell reduces routine finishing work, while grooved and square-edge profiles serve different fastening and edge-detail needs.

Trex Select offers a more restrained grain pattern and a 35-year residential fade-and-stain warranty. Its newer Whiskey Barrel, Malted Barley and Millstone colors include heat-mitigating technology; that feature does not apply automatically to every Select color.

Trex Enhance uses a scalloped underside to reduce board weight. Ten colors span solid and blended looks, with heat-mitigating technology on Cinnamon Cove, Golden Hour, Honey Grove, Pebble Beach and Tide Pool.

Trex Refuge is PVC decking, with a wire-brushed surface in Martis Valley and Point Reyes. Its published Class A flame-spread rating concerns this decking product; it is different from a roof-assembly fire classification and does not make a home fireproof.

children.text: A slender aluminum frame and vertical balusters keep the perimeter visually light. Compare post positions and stair transitions alongside the rail finish so the entire run reads as one system.

Glass infill opens sightlines while the surrounding aluminum frame defines each section. Panel sizing, support and stair details need to be planned together; glass is a distinct infill choice, not a substitute inserted into an unrelated rail kit.

Mesh infill gives the deck a more architectural, industrial appearance. The perimeter frame remains part of the design, with dedicated infill and mounting components selected for level and stair sections.

Horizontal rods create long visual lines across the deck edge. Rail sections, posts and stair components must be selected as the Rod Rail assembly rather than mixed with cable or vertical-baluster parts.

Cable infill offers an open view with narrow horizontal lines. End conditions, cable connections and the supporting posts are central to the system, so the layout should be resolved before deck boards and post locations are finalized.

catalogItems.title: Trex Signature X-Series frameless glass railing

children.text: Frameless glass places the emphasis on the view beyond the deck. The glass panels and supporting X-Series posts work as a specified assembly, with the stair and corner arrangements considered alongside the level runs.

Transcend provides a substantial, traditional rail profile with coordinated posts, caps and infill choices. It suits a deck where the railing is a visible design feature rather than a minimal outline.

Select Classic combines familiar rail proportions with metal balusters. Review the rail and post colors as an assembly, including the stair sections, rather than choosing parts from photographs of different configurations.

The T-shaped top rail gives this Select option a distinct hand profile. Its rails, reinforcement and balusters are a specific configuration; the connections should be reviewed with the posts and stair layout.

Select aluminum railing offers a metal alternative within the Select range. Its slim sections suit a clean perimeter, with matching rail kits, mounting hardware and gates considered as a complete layout.

Select mesh changes the look of the infill while retaining a defined perimeter rail. The mesh panels and accessory kits should be matched to their specified rail and post assembly, including separate stair details.

Enhance steel railing provides a simple metal perimeter with a more open view than broad solid rails. Consider its finish, mounting hardware and stair kits together when comparing it with the composite Enhance option.
Enhance composite railing uses a traditional top-and-bottom rail arrangement. It is a separate choice from Enhance steel railing, with its own rails, post sleeves and installation components.

children.text: Fascia covers the deck rim and gives stair edges a finished appearance. It is a vertical finishing board, not the structural rim joist or a substitute for walking-surface decking. Dedicated fascia fasteners accommodate movement without treating the board like a deck plank.

Hideaway includes fastening choices for grooved decking, face-fastened boards and fascia. Hidden clips attach at the board edges; screws and plugs address other locations. Selecting the fastener by board profile and application avoids using a fascia connection in the walking surface.

Deck lighting helps define steps, railings and the edges of outdoor living areas after dark. Plan fixture locations, wiring access and the power supply before enclosing posts or finishing the underside of the deck.

RainEscape collects water below the deck boards and directs it away through troughs and downspouts. It is most useful when you want to use the space under an elevated deck. Drainage routing and access need to be resolved before the walking surface is installed.

LWG 3” Metal Plates are used to mechanically attach insulation, cover boards and base sheets to lightweight insulating concrete (LWIC) and gypsum decks. The LWG 3” Metal Plate is a circular design with one center fastener placement hole and eight equally spaced fastener placement holes around the perimeter of the plate allowing for maximum versatility. Required pullout values can be achieved by installing multiple LWG Fasteners in one LWG 3” Metal Plate.

The 3” TL Insulation Plate is used to attach roof insulation, coverboards and BUR base sheets to cementitious wood fiber, gypsum and lightweight concrete substrates. Use with MuleHide TL Roofing Fastener.

All Purpose Bar is designed for use as an anchor bar for attachment of MuleHide EPDM membranes. May be installed in the field seam as a batten bar and used at the base of curbs, parapet walls and angle changes as an anchor bar. Also be used with any MuleHide single-ply membranes as a termination bar. Refer to the MuleHide Single-Ply Manuals for specific use and installation instructions.

Drill Point Fasteners (#12) are specifically engineered to secure insulation, coverboards and base sheets to corrugated steel (16 – 22 ga.) and wood substrates. Featuring a #2 double flute self-drilling point and exclusive tapered entry thread design, penetrating steel quickly and offering exceptional back-out resistance. Available with #3 Phillips Head.

EHD Fastener (#15) is engineered for lap attachment to corrugated steel (18 – 22 ga.) and wood substrates in higher wind uplift roof assemblies. Featuring a #2 double flute self-drilling point and exclusive tapered entry thread design, penetrating steel quickly and offering exceptional back-out resistance.

HDP Fastener (#14) is engineered to secure insulation, coverboards, base sheets and single-ply roof membrane systems to corrugated steel (16 - 22 ga.), wood, and concrete substrates. Featuring a #2 double flute self-drilling point and exclusive tapered entry thread design, penetrating steel quickly and offering exceptional back-out resistance.

Cardboard Discs are used when induction weld systems are being installed over expanded or extruded polystyrene insulation to prevent the plates from melting the insulation or cause depressions in the insulation which can lead to ponding and ultimately roof damage.

Induction Weld Plates are approximately 3-3/8" in diameter. Plates are approved for use with steel, wood or structural concrete roof decks. The Induction Weld Plates can be installed using #15 EHD, Tru-Spike Fasteners, and PFC Purlin Drill Point Fasteners.

LWG Fasteners are engineered to secure insulation, cover boards and base sheets to lightweight insulating concrete (LWIC) and gypsum decks. The LWG Fastener features an exclusive thread design engineered for exceptional pullout. When used in conjunction with the LWG 3” Metal Plate, multiple fasteners can be installed to achieve the required minimum pullout.

children.text: The MuleHide Zamac Nailin™ Roofing Fastener is a nail-drive, general purpose anchor that can be used in concrete, block, brick, or stone. Applications include attachment of roof membrane terminations, roof flashing, and mechanical/electrical fixtures. It features an anchor body formed from a corrosion resistant zamac alloy with a carbon steel drive nail. The mushroom head provides a tamperproof installation. Note: The Zamac Nailin Roofing Fastener is not recommended for overhead, life-safety or sustained tensile loading applications unless special considerations are given to the allowable loads.

PFC Purlin Drill Point (#12) is a self-drilling fastener engineered to secure single-ply roofing membrane to structural steel purlins (16 ga. to 3/16") in standing seam metal roof recover applications. The specially designed 3/4" long pilot point prevents the existing metal roof panel from jacking up the threads during the drilling operation, thereby reducing point burnout and breakage.

Pre-Assembled Fastener System offers a simple, economical and ergonomic “system solution” to increase the productivity in the mechanical attachment of roof insulation boards. The system includes a pre-assembled Drill Point Fastener (#12) with Phillips head style and 3" Galvalume Plate or a Drill Point Fastener (#12) with 1/4" Hex head style and 3" Recessed Galvalume Plate, a Magnetic Setter Tool, 29" Stand-up Electric Power tool and a Canvas Fastener Bag.

TB-90 Termination Bar is made from special extruded aluminum without sharp edges providing a smooth flat surface with no ledge against the roofing material.

TL Fastener is designed to mechanically attach rigid insulation board and single-ply membrane to structural cement wood fiber, gypsum and lightweight insulating concrete roof decks. Features a high-thread profile with a tapered root diameter and sharp point. Its unique design allows it to penetrate the roof deck and progressively compact the base material, creating a stronger hold in weak material. Used in conjunction with the 2" TL Seam Plate and 3" TL Insulation Plate.

Tru-Spike Fastener is a one-piece, vibration-resistant anchor designed to attach insulation, single-ply roofing, wood and steel to structural concrete roof decks and walls. Featuring an “S” shaped configuration at the working end to create an expansion mechanism, it provides a fast, reliable fastening solution for roof applications over structural concrete surfaces.

These components are factory fabricated from Blue Ridge Fiberboard Structodek insulation board. The Cant Strips are cut at angles that provide a true 45-degree angle between horizontal and vertical surfaces. The Tapered Edge is cut on angles that slope from zero on one edge to ½” to 2″ thickness on the opposite edge.

DensDeck Prime Roof Boards by Georgia-Pacific Gypsum are a patented design features a gypsum core with embedded glass mat facers on the top and bottom of the board. DensDeck Prime can be used in a variety of commercial roof systems and provides an excellent thermal barrier as well as exceptional fire, moisture, and wind uplift resistance properties.

children.text: DensDeck ProFast Prime 3/8” roof board is an innovative, lightweight roofing solution designed to enhance performance, efficiency, and cost savings in roofing applications. Approximately 20% lighter than ½” DensDeck Prime Roof Board, it offers enhanced maneuverability, making easier to transport, handle and install without compromising strength, durability, or dimensional stability.

DensDeck® Roof Boards by Georgia-Pacific Gypsum are utilized in a wide variety of roofing systems for new and re-roofing applications as cover boards and thermal barriers. Featuring a combination of fire resistance, strength and dimensional stability, DensDeck roof boards enhance the performance of all roofing assemblies and are widely respected by leading roofing system manufacturers and consultants.

children.text: DensDeck® StormX Prime Roof Boards by Georgia-Pacific Gypsum are a reinforced gypsum cover board with an enhanced, moisture-resistant core and coated glass mat facers. DensDeck StormX is extremely durable and is approved for use in assemblies meeting FM’s Very Severe Hail (VSH) Classification.

Flat Roof Insulation provides high long-term R-Values and saves labor installation time. Suitable for use with all roofing membrane materials, expanded polystyrene (EPS) roof insulation is compatible with loose-laid and attached single-ply membranes, conventional built-up roofing or modified bitumen systems. Flat Roof Insulation is unfaced EPS and is suitable for use with loosely laid single-ply membranes. Flat EPS Roof Insulation is also used with conventional BUR and mechanically or adhesively attached single-ply and modified bitumen membranes when field-applied cover boards are used.

Tapered Roof Insulation was developed more than 30 years ago with a dual purpose in mind: to drain and insulate dead-level roof decks. Manufactured from lightweight EPS, Tapered Roof Insulation is a value-engineered system that has been proven in new and reroof applications all over the country. This tapered roof insulation technology creates high thermal performance which improves interior comfort and reduces the energy costs of keeping a building comfortable.

MuleHide Poly ISO 1-HD is 1/2" thick, 100 psi high density polyisocyanurate insulation board specifically designed for use as a cover board. Consists of a closed-cell polyisocyanurate foam core laminated to premium performance coated glass fiber felt facers. MuleHide Poly ISO 1-HD is designed for use as a cover board over roof insulation boards or existing membranes. Compatible with single-ply roofing systems (ballasted, mechanically attached and fully adhered) and modified bitumen roofing systems, on new construction, tearoff and recover (retrofit) projects. Suitable for use with approved fasteners and plates, and low-rise foam adhesive. Poly ISO 1-HD can achieve a FM hail resistance rating of SH-1 with certain membranes.

MuleHide Poly ISO 1-HD Plus is an FM-approved, ½” thick high density polyisocyanurate insulation board that was specifically designed for use as a cover board in fully adhered systems. Suitable for both re-roofing and new construction applications, Poly ISO 1-HD Plus consists of a closed-cell polyisocyanurate foam core laminated to premium performance coated glass fiber felt facers. Poly ISO HD-1 Plus has an R-value of 2.5, which is significantly higher than roof cover boards made with other materials such as wood fiber or gypsum.

MuleHide Poly ISO 1-HD80 is a ½" thick, high-density polyisocyanurate insulation board that was specifically designed for use as a cover board with mechanically attached and induction welded single-ply roofing systems only. Suitable for use with approved fasteners and plates. This product consists of a closed-cell polyisocyanurate foam. In addition to providing a durable underlayment for roofing membranes, Poly ISO 1-HD80 has an R-value of 2.5 which is significantly higher than that of other cover board products such as wood fiber or gypsum.

MuleHide Poly ISO Flat insulations consist of a closed-cell polyisocyanurate foam core laminated to heavy, (non-asphaltic) glass fiber reinforced felt facers. The product insulations are compatible with all MuleHide membranes and accessories and are available in 20 and 25 psi densities. MuleHide Poly ISO insulation boards may be used for ballasted, mechanically attached and fully adhered single-ply roofing systems. Poly ISO insulation board may be installed over approved decks and substrates on new construction, tearoffs and recover (retrofit) projects. Rated for use in UL Class A and FM Class 1 assemblies.

Securock® roof boards provide exceptional bond and low absorption in adhered systems and with its homogenous composition achieves high wind-uplift ratings with no risk of facer delamination. Made from 97% recycled material, Securock® roof boards combine superior performance with sustainable design for all types of roofing systems including single-ply, fluid-applied, built-up, spray foam, metal and modified bitumen roofing.

Accommodates single pipe sizes from 1" to 6" in diameter. Conical-shaped steps securely seal all single pipe penetrations. ShapeShift® pitch pans consist of straight and outside corner sections that snap together to create an endless number of pitch pan sizes to seal around roof projections. The radius corner pieces measure approximately 2" x 2". The straight sections measure approximately 3" long. The high-strength polymer pieces have a 2-1/2" base flange with a 1-3/4" high side. The pieces snap together with interlocking joints. The smallest pitch pan possible is 4" x 4" (4 corner pieces). The maximum size is unlimited. ShapeShift® pitch pans are approved for installation on MuleHide warranted projects when installed on vertical surfaces if filled with JTS 1 sealant instead of MP Liquid Sealant.

Primarily used to seal details where field fabrication is necessary, such as drain details, pipe flashings, pitch pocket flashings, seaming joints of the MuleHide TPO Coated Metal and any place where reinforced membrane is not practical.

Prefabricated two-way, or static, vents allow proper ventilation of attic spaces below TPO membranes. The reinforced membrane flange allows for quick installation by centering vent over opening and welding to the field membrane.

A 24-gauge galvanized steel sheet coated with a layer of 0.035" non-reinforced TPO flashing. Uniform in shape and size and provide watertightness at inside corners formed by TPO coated metal and/or TPO flashing membrane. Provides a neat, finished look to building corners, curbs and parapet flashings with no cutting required.

Interlocking, two-piece prefabricated pockets of non-reinforced TPO material used to seal pipe clusters or other irregular shaped penetrations. Pockets length can be adjusted from 7-1/2" to 11-1/2" by following the pre-molded cutting lines.

Uniform in shape and size and provide water tightness at outside corners formed by TPO coated metal and/or TPO flashing membrane. Provides a neat, finished look to building corners, curbs and parapet flashings with no cutting required.

Contains a split (cut) and overlap tab that allows the pipe boot to be opened and wrapped around a round pipe with an obstruction. Such obstructions prevent the use of a standard pre-molded pipe boot.

A split (cut) and overlap tab are incorporated into these parts to allow the flashing to be opened and wrapped around a square penetration with an obstruction. The TPO Square Tubing Wraps are primarily used to seal details where field fabrication is necessary, such as drain details, pipe flashings and pitch pocket flashings.
Used to seal step-offs at splice intersections. Installation is mandatory on all 60 mil and 80 mil TPO systems and on 45 mil systems where step-offs have not been properly sealed.

Uniform in shape and size and provide watertightness at corners formed by TPO coated metal and/or TPO flashing membrane. Provides a neat, finished look to building corners, curbs and parapet flashings with no cutting or stretching required.
